chunks: He said: Ahmad ibn Ali narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ismail from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said: I heard Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) say:
So and so [the Banu Abbas] would arrest and imprison me. Then he said: Although this matter would be much prolonged, but it would end in a nice way.

key_terms.إِلَى سَلَامَةٍ: To safety / ending in a good outcome
key_terms.بَنِي فُلَانٍ: So and so / The Banu [a placeholder for a specific tribe or family, here referring to the Abbasids]

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Musa al-Kadhim say about his imprisonment?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights Imam Musa al-Kadhim’s (a.s.) prophetic awareness of his prolonged detention by the Abbasids, framing it as a divinely ordained trial leading to ultimate safety (*salama*). It serves as a key evidence for his Imamate, demonstrating his knowledge of the unseen (*ghayb*) and his patience during the era of the Waqifiya, who awaited his return. The mention of 'Banu Flan' (a specific clan, often identified as the Banu Ma'ruf or Abbasid officials) underscores the political tension of the time.
